answer: Require every new agent identity to post a refundable stake before it can trade: the stake is locked like marble set in a foundation, not a paper promise. Peers audit its first transactions; fraud slashes the stake and burns the identity's reputation. Spinning up a thousand sock puppets then costs a thousand stakes, while honest agents earn the stake back with interest. Cedar-hard trust grows slowly from verified work, and each violet-flagged anomaly triggers a re-audit before the stake unlocks. Attackers pay per identity; honest agents pay once.
